A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Nordic countries have a strong common background in the egalitarian comprehensive school and in the Nordic welfare state.
the Nordic school evaluation policies are not only about accountability and transparency but also about the discursive practices of educational governance.
the current Nordic QAE policies and the discursive justifications for them reflect a global trend towards accountability and transparency in education, but with country-specific nuances.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Nordic countries, although sharing a common educational history and a similar political culture, have adopted different approaches in their school evaluation policies and practices.
the Nordic discursive triad is not static, but rather dynamic.
, in spite of their similarities, the Nordic countries have developed their own discursive rationales on the school evaluation and transparency policies.
